result.title: Learning When to Think: Dual-Reference Offline Optimization for Adaptive VLM Reasoning
result.summary: Reasoning traces improve vision-language models on complex multimodal tasks, but forcing every input to follow a long reasoning process leads to overthinking and unnecessary inference cost. We study adaptive fast/slow thinking for VLMs, where one model answers directly for simple inputs and reasons step by step when needed. Fast answers and slow traces often come from distinct behavior policies, making a single-reference offline objective misweight one mode. We propose DUAL-REFERENCE BOLT (DR-BOLT), which distinguishes the desired fast/slow mixture reference from the sampling distribution and corrects their mismatch in reward-weighted training. Fast/slow partition competition explains routing in the optimal target; an efficient source-wise correction approximates the exact objective when response formats are well separated. Matched Qwen3-VL comparisons use identical candidate banks to isolate the objective from slow-teacher quality. DR-BOLT improves score-length trade-offs over the evaluated offline and online baselines on ScienceQA and three held-out transfer benchmarks, with a 24.1% cross-benchmark slow ratio and a 2.90-fold end-to-end training speedup over reproduced GRPO. These results support adaptive reasoning in the studied two-reference setting, while broader robustness remains open. Our code is available at https://github.com/HongbinLin3589/DR-BOLT.

AI.brief_summary: 研究 VLM 的自适应快/慢思考，提出双参考离线优化方法 DR-BOLT：把期望的快慢混合参考分布与采样分布区分开，在奖励加权训练中修正二者错配，使模型对简单输入直接作答、必要时才展开长推理。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应「何时思考」的停止/路由决策与推理成本权衡，但其核心是离线训练目标与贡献分配而非 latent 状态生成；其快慢划分竞争与跨基准 slow ratio 可供核查停止决策的行为证据。
